PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:30 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called meeting to order 5:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Sucessor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:31 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor agency reconvened to open session at 6:10 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on item #1 - staff made a presentation, the City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on this item.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Aragumedo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:20 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Vice Mayor Altamirano offered the invocation

PUBLIC COMMENT




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano

4.. 2024-2029 Municipal Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department

3.. Approval of Public Safety Pink Patch Program

2.. Approval of Minutes

1.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 4A, 4B and 4C

SCHEDULED MATTERS

5.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte provided an overview for the two weeks.

6.. Approval of Two Additional Part-Time Positions and Funding for the Parks and Recreation Department  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Mireya Garcia Parks and Recreation Director Alaniz provided an overview of the staff report. 

In response to Councilmember Garcia's inquiry about the timeline for hiring the two new instructors, Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz stated that the process would take approximately two months.



PUBLIC HEARING

7.. 2021-2029 Housing Element Update and Negative Declaration  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez 

Acting Director of Economic Development and Planning Morales provided a brief overview, followed by a PowerPoint presentation from Veronica Tang of Tang and Associates.



Councilmember Lainez mentioned that he attended one of the community meetings and asked about the process if the Council adopts the Housing Element and it later returns with corrections. Veronica Tang responded that the draft has been submitted to the State, and they have not yet received any comments. If the draft comes back with changes, it would be brought back to the City Council, and minor changes could be handled by staff. In response to Councilmember Lainez's question about whether the City would still maintain control over which projects are implemented with the adoption of the Housing Element, Veronica Tang assured him that the Housing Element supports and enables the City to maintain local control.



In response to Mayor Argumedo's question about consulting the Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) on future projects, Veronica Tang explained that DTSC oversight would be determined on a project-by-project basis, as it is impossible to predict which projects would require DTSC involvement.



When Councilmember Garcia inquired whether there were any changes to the existing Housing policy, Veronica Tang confirmed that there were none.



Mayor Argumedo then opened the Public Hearing. As no individuals wished to address the City Council on this item, Mayor Argumedo closed the Public Hearing.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia reported attending the Contract Cities Conference as well as the street dedication for Haig Papaian Jr.



Councilmember Lainez reported on attending the Gateway Cities Annual Retreat, noting the valuable information from the Empower Gateway Cities meeting, where SoCal Edison introduced Empower Gateway and provided subsidies beneficial to Commerce residents. He also attended the Contract Cities Fall Seminar, where discussions included Measure A, a housing-related measure that will be on the ballot. Additionally, he participated in the Haig Papaian Jr. street dedication ceremony today, commending staff for organizing an excellent event.



Vice Mayor Altamirano reported attending both the Contract Cities Seminar and the Haig Papaian Jr. street dedication ceremony.

Mayor Argumedo reported on attending the Haig Papaian Jr. ceremony, reflecting on his long-standing relationship with the casino since 1996. He highlighted Haig Papaian’s significant contributions to the scholarship program, particularly his role in increasing the funding. Mayor Argumedo also discussed SB 549, expressing hope that it will be vetoed.



ADJOURNMENT

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoyotl requested that the Senior Citizen Commission and the senior social club adhere to established procedures and comply with the Brown Act.



Pedro Gilis, Irma Vargas, Myra Garcia, Fabian Crisanto, and Patricia Duenes requested that Spanish translation services be provided at City Council meetings and that staff respond to the emails they have sent.



Jasmin Gonzalez, representing a group of citizens, asked for the opportunity to meet with the Councilmembers.



Josie Betancort expressed concerns about the potential loss of parking for residents and requested that this issue be placed on the agenda and resolved.



Randy Sax Romero inquired about the status of the Modelo project and developments at Veteran's Park.
